subject: function:next_boss_hint
value:
THE RUN-28 NAME-BOUND RELOCATION-HASH MIGRATION UPDATED webfrank.py AND wf_rederive_pin.py AND LEFT EVERY OTHER DERIVER BEHIND, SO THE WHOLE PERMUTATION-RULE DERIVATION PATH HAS BEEN DEAD FOR ANY WINDOW CONTAINING A RELOCATION -- AND IT FAILS AS A CRASH THAT READS LIKE A PROPERTY OF THE FUNCTION.

MECHANISM. `webfrank._relocation_sha256(relocations, symbols=None)` was changed to hash the symbol NAME instead of the ELF r_info INDEX, because the index is TU-global and renumbers on any unrelated edit (measured on gauntworld::fn_8005FB48). The new signature REFUSES a relocation whose name it was not given: `raise ValueError("relocation hash needs the symbol name for the relocation at +0x%x")`. The derivers all feed it `raw_region_records()`, which yields only (offset, info, addend) TRIPLES and no names. So every derivation over a window carrying at least one relocation raised, while windows with no relocation kept working perfectly -- the empty-list hash is unchanged. That split is what made the defect invisible: the failure is data-dependent, not systematic.

MEASURED SCOPE at the time of writing: wf_rederive_pin.py was migrated (it passes window_syms/moved_syms and is the correct reference). SIX call sites were not -- ch_derive.py, cn_derive.py, cn_search.py, ha_close.py (_perm_entry), tools/gdl/build_rule.py and composed_census/build_rule_pw.py. ch_derive and ha_close are repaired by the commit that asserts this law (ch_derive.region_symbols / moved_symbols, reproducing exactly the mapping apply_patch builds for `our_symbols`); the other four are REPORTED, not touched, because tools/gdl is another lane's this run.

WHY THIS IS A LAW AND NOT A BUG REPORT. The canary caught it and nothing else could have. ch_canary replays four SHIPPED derivations and requires byte-identical orders; calc_wizard_pos passed (its window carries no relocation) and next_boss_hint CRASHED. A lane that skipped the canary would have read the crash -- or, worse, the sweep's blanket `except Exception: continue`, which silently drops the row -- as 'this function does not close', and recorded a cap on a function the deriver never actually examined. hv_sweep.triage swallows exactly this exception. So the corollary is the operative rule: A DERIVATION THAT CANNOT RUN IS NOT A NEGATIVE RESULT, and any census whose inner loop catches Exception broadly must be canaried before its refusals are believed. Discipline 14 generalises from guards to TOOLS: a crash is a measurement of the tool.

COST OF THE OMISSION, stated so the migration checklist is concrete: after the repair, the same sweep that had been returning refusals produced two byte-exact closes on its first run. The migration needed one more step -- grep every caller of the changed function -- and skipping it cost at least one run of harvest yield.
